trust_decision.summary: Decided once, at the boundary where a string enters evaluation: template-variable declarations and template-authored payload text are SOURCE and may be rendered, while values coming from runtime data, CLI options, constants and the cross-protocol template context are DATA and must never be re-scanned or compiled. The pinned code has no such notion: expressions.evaluate substitutes map values into the expression string before govaluate compiles it (expressions.go:58-61), and variables.EvaluateWithInteractsh uses an already-present runtime value as the string to evaluate (variables.go:117-124).

landing_point.why: The advisory names DAST/fuzz mode; the fuzz rule merges response/runtime values into input.Values and then re-evaluates every value of that map (execute.go:222-257), which is the first place an engineer reading the summary looks.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Matchers are not DAST/fuzz payload rendering: the advisory is about fuzzing mode, the DSL expression is template-authored, and the response value only appears as a literal inside an already-quoted string, so it reads as a matcher-semantics question rather than the fuzzing disclosure.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A runtime value must still shadow a declared template variable (server-issued login token replaces a declared empty token; a server-edited upload filename replaces the initial one) - it just must stop being rendered as template text.

O6_input_shapes: raw {{interactsh-url}} vs fully percent-encoded %7B%7Binteractsh-url%7D%7D vs mixed raw/encoded brace pairs
runtime value substituted inside a single-quoted vs double-quoted DSL string literal
{{name}} parenthesis marker vs the general section marker form
scalar string value vs []interface{} slice payload (slices are copied, never evaluated)
value strings containing quotes, backslashes, newlines, tabs and carriage returns
template-authored helper call wrapping a marker, e.g. {{url_encode('{{interactsh-url}}')}}
marker that only appears after a first render pass, i.e. produced by a payload/variable indirection
